cohort: Women who delivered in 16 California hospitals between July 2012 and June 2013
finding: A significant proportion of women with severe morbidity (42.5%) delivered preterm, with 17.8% delivering <32 weeks, and those with placental hemorrhage had a high rate (63%) of prior cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: 75% of women with placental hemorrhage delivered preterm, and 63% of these women had a prior cesarean delivery, highlighting the risk of subsequent preterm delivery associated with cesarean delivery.
gest_age: Preterm delivery was significantly more common in SMM women compared to SMM-negative women (41 vs 8%; P < .0001), including delivery <32 weeks (18 vs 2%; P < .0001).
